opportunities.title: Small Research Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: BES membership required; open to researchers from all countries globally (projects can be conducted anywhere); further criteria for PhD students; does not cover salary of principal researcher, bench fees or departmental vehicle hire; not for completing undergraduate/masters degrees or funded fellowships.
opportunities.summary: Provides up to £5,000 for new and innovative ecological research of the highest international standard.

opportunities.title: Synthesis Grants

amount.raw: up to £30,000 over two years for groups of 8-15 participants

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Main applicant must have BES membership; working groups of 8-15 individuals with diverse mix of career stages, institutions and international participation; groups should not be formed entirely of academic institution members.
opportunities.summary: Fast-tracking innovative and impactful research by contributing up to £30k towards the formation of new two-year synthesis groups that bring together diverse interdisciplinary groups to analyse and synthesise existing data.

opportunities.title: Long-term Research Grants

amount.raw: £500 per year for 10 years; £3,500 claimable in year 1; additional £3,500 claimable in year 6

opportunities.eligibility_summary: BES membership required; open to all types of ecologists including conservation practitioners (Reserve Managers, consultants) and university academics; awarded to individuals, not organisations.
opportunities.summary: Provides funding over 10 years for long-term ecological studies anywhere in the world, enabling existing short-term projects with 1-2 years of data to be funded into the long term (ecological restoration, habitat creation, alien species control, climate change).

opportunities.title: Pedagogical Research and Development Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: BES membership required; open to anyone involved in teaching ecology at any level (early years to lifelong learning, formal or informal); awarded to individuals, not organisations; no geographical restrictions; funding not available for work forming part of a degree/masters/PhD/fellowship.
opportunities.summary: Funds research informing teaching and learning practices in ecology (up to £5k) to improve learners' experience and promote excellence in teaching, including evidence-based innovative practice, systematic reviews, and emerging education research.

opportunities.title: Connecting Ecologists with Other Disciplines Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: BES membership required; open to PhD students, postdoctoral fellows, early career ecologists, established researchers or employees of other organisations; not open to undergraduates and masters students; awarded to individuals, not organisations; placements up to 12 months.
opportunities.summary: Promoting interdisciplinary skills by funding up to £20k towards placements in different disciplines and sectors, immersing an ecologist in another professional world where ecology can make a difference.

opportunities.title: Outreach and Engagement Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Lead applicant must have BES membership; open to individuals, teams and organisations across all experience levels; no restrictions on where applicants come from or carry out work; proposals must target a non-academic audience.
opportunities.summary: Provides funding of up to £2,000 for individuals, teams and organisations to engage public audiences with the excitement, importance and relevance of ecological science through outreach, public engagement and science communication.

opportunities.title: Training and Travel Grants

amount.raw: maximum £250 for virtual conferences/courses registration; maximum £500 for in-person events

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must be a BES member and a PhD student or postgraduate researcher (postdoc researchers, undergraduates and masters students not eligible); must work/study at a university or research institution; at least three years must pass before applying again after a previous award.
opportunities.summary: Helps PhD students and postgraduate researchers meet the costs of specialist field training courses and the travel costs associated with presenting their work at workshops and conferences.

opportunities.title: Annual Meeting Grants 2026
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must be a BES member at any career stage; must be a citizen of and based in the Global South; must be travelling from and returning to their Global South country; must have applied to present at the Annual Meeting; at least three years since last BES Training and Travel Grant.
opportunities.summary: Supports researchers based in Global South countries to attend the BES Annual Meeting 2026 in the UK, covering costs directly related to attending the meeting (registration, transport, food, accommodation) up to £1,000.
